note: The reported symptom is 'Internal compiler error: access violation. Attempted to read from address 0x0000000000000009' -- dxc failing inside itself, not DXIL validation rejecting a shader. Keyed on internal-failure exit status rather than on the message, because the same defect wears different faces per build: the assert-enabled Debug ground truth traps the clang assert(!isIncompleteType()) that tex3d identified (0x80000003 / 0xE0000001), while the Release release-binaries the reporter used have that assert compiled out and access-violate instead (0xC0000005). A predicate matching either message would score the other build clean and manufacture a 'fixed' verdict. Deliberately NOT 'nonzero exit': on Windows an ordinary diagnosed error, an invalid profile and a DXIL validation failure all exit E_FAIL (0x80004005), and this issue's title says 'validation', so the E_FAIL cases must NOT count. Controls: control-good-vertex.hlsl (a well-formed vs shader with the same struct-with-SV_ClipDistance shape, --expect no-match) proves the predicate does not fire on a clean compile; control-sized-array.hlsl (the same repro with the two incomplete array decls given explicit bounds, --expect no-match) proves it is the incomplete array type and not the shader's other invalidity; control-syntax-error.hlsl (--expect no-match) proves an ordinary E_FAIL diagnostic does not score as an internal failure.
